shares fell 2% in premarket trading on Monday after the PC and printer giant said it believes the computer industry will decline mid-single digits next year.

"Consistent with current third-party industry forecasts, HP’s preliminary planning assumption is that industry-wide personal computer unit volumes decline roughly mid-single-digits in percentage terms in calendar year 2027 as compared to calendar year 2026," the company

in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. "This planning assumption is dependent on market performance in the second half of calendar 2026, which remains fluid, and is subject to change."
HP added that the disclosure does not mean it is providing financial guidance for 2027.
